headline: Gateway Hudson Tunnel project reaches first boring milestone
dek: The first pair of machines will bore about a mile through the Palisades in New Jersey before crews begin the Hudson River section of the long-delayed rail project.
body: The Gateway Development Commission marked the start of tunnel boring for the Hudson Tunnel Project on Monday, moving a long-delayed rail connection between New Jersey and New York into its first excavation phase.

Officials said the first tunnel-boring machine will begin digging in the coming days after final testing. A second machine is expected to follow soon. Together, the machines will cut about 5,100 feet through hard rock beneath the Palisades from a portal in North Bergen to an access shaft near the border of Weehawken and Hoboken.

The machines are designed to advance roughly 30 feet per day, with scheduled maintenance pauses, and are expected to reach the access shaft in about a year. They will then be removed so a second pair of machines can build the portions of the two-tube tunnel beneath the Hudson River, according to the commission's project release.

The first phase is part of a larger plan to build a new two-track rail tunnel and rehabilitate the existing North River Tunnel, which has been in service since 1910. The Gateway Development Commission said the current tunnel is a major source of delays for hundreds of thousands of daily passengers, while New Jersey officials say the new connection will eventually double rail capacity between the states.

The milestone follows nearly three years of construction preparation, including work under Tonnelle Avenue to create room for the boring machines. News 12 New Jersey reported that each machine is about 28 feet tall and 500 feet long. The project is expected to improve reliability along the Northeast Corridor, but its full benefits will depend on the completion of the remaining construction packages and the river crossing.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Gateway Hudson Tunnel Project Reaches Boring Milestone
